answer: An agent economy can defend against Sybil farms by tying identity weights to a decentralized trust graph where each vertex requires verified hardware-backed collateral. New participants must lock a durable ferrous staking deposit, and their transaction trees are pruned like timber if cyclic coordination patterns are detected across pseudonyms. This forces an attacker to purchase non-fungible hardware and lock substantial capital per created identity, imposing an insurmountable cost that scales linearly with swarm size.
